text: For pulsating DC voltages (alternating voltages without change of polarity) the DC threshold shall be applied when assessing the specific voltage condition.
condition: pulsating DC voltages

text: The "H" point for each seat shall be determined in accordance with the procedure described in Annex 6.
When the protective system for the front seating positions includes belts, the belt components shall meet the requirements of Regulation No. 16.
condition: protective system for front seating positions includes belts

text: Seating positions where a dummy is installed and the protective system includes belts shall be provided with anchorage points conforming to Regulation No. 14.
condition: dummy installed and protective system includes belts

text: The test of the vehicle carried out in accordance with Annex 3 shall be considered satisfactory only if all the conditions of paragraphs 5.2.1. to 5.2.7. are satisfied at the same time.
Vehicles equipped with electric power train shall additionally meet the requirements of paragraph 5.2.8.
condition: vehicle equipped with electric power train

text: The requirements of paragraph 5.2.8. may be met by a separate impact test at the request of the manufacturer and after validation by the Technical Service only provided that the electrical components do not influence the occupant protection performance as defined in paragraphs 5.2.1. to 5.2.5.
condition: separate impact test for electrical safety requested by manufacturer

text: In a separate impact test for paragraph 5.2.8., the requirements shall be checked according to Annex 3 except paragraphs 2., 5. and 6. of Annex 3, but a Hybrid III dummy fitted with a 45° ankle and meeting its adjustment specifications shall be installed in each of the front outboard seats.
condition: separate impact test for electrical safety

text: The performance criteria on the dummies in the front outboard seats shall be recorded in accordance with Annex 8.
The head performance criterion (HPC) recorded on the dummies in the front outboard seats shall not exceed 1,000.
The resultant head acceleration of the front outboard dummies shall not exceed 80 g for more than 3 ms, calculated cumulatively, excluding rebound movement of the head.
The Injury Criteria for the neck (NIC) of the front outboard dummies shall not exceed the values shown in Figure 1 (neck tension criterion).
The Injury Criteria for the neck (NIC) of the front outboard dummies shall not exceed the values shown in Figure 2 (neck shear criterion).
The neck bending moment about the y axis of the front outboard dummies shall not exceed 57 Nm in extension.
The Thorax Compression Criterion (ThCC) of the front outboard dummies shall not exceed 42 mm.
The viscous criterion (V * C) for the thorax of the front outboard dummies shall not exceed 1,0 m/s.
The femur force criterion (FFC) of the front outboard dummies shall not exceed the force-time performance criterion shown in Figure 3.
The tibia compression force criterion (TCFC) of the front outboard dummies shall not exceed 8 kN.
The tibia index (TI) of the front outboard dummies, measured at the top and bottom of each tibia, shall not exceed 1,3 at either location.
The movement of the sliding knee joints of the front outboard dummies shall not exceed 15 mm.
Following the test, the residual steering wheel displacement measured at the centre of the steering wheel hub shall not exceed 80 mm in the upwards vertical direction.
Following the test, the residual steering wheel displacement measured at the centre of the steering wheel hub shall not exceed 100 mm in the rearward horizontal direction.
During the test no door shall open.

For automatically activated door locking systems installed optionally and/or de-activatable by the driver, the no-door-opening requirement shall be verified using one of the two test procedures of paragraphs 5.2.3.1.1. or 5.2.3.1.2., at the choice of the manufacturer.
condition: automatically activated door locking system installed optionally and/or can be de-activated by the driver

text: If testing according to Annex 3, paragraph 1.4.3.5.2.1., the manufacturer shall additionally demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Technical Service (e.g. in-house data) that, in the absence of the system or when it is de-activated, no door will open in case of the impact.
condition: optional/de-activatable automatic door locking system tested per Annex 3 paragraph 1.4.3.5.2.1.

text: Alternatively, the no-door-opening test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 3, paragraph 1.4.3.5.2.2.
condition: optional/de-activatable automatic door locking system, manufacturer's choice of procedure

text: After the impact, the side doors shall be unlocked.
In vehicles equipped with an automatically activated door locking system, the doors shall be locked before the moment of impact and be unlocked after the impact.
condition: vehicle equipped with an automatically activated door locking system

text: For automatically activated door locking systems installed optionally and/or de-activatable by the driver, the side-door unlocking requirement shall be verified using one of the two test procedures of paragraphs 5.2.4.2.1. or 5.2.4.2.2., at the choice of the manufacturer.
condition: automatically activated door locking system installed optionally and/or can be de-activated by the driver

text: If testing according to Annex 3, paragraph 1.4.3.5.2.1., the manufacturer shall additionally demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Technical Service (e.g. in-house data) that, in the absence of the system or when it is de-activated, no locking of the side doors occurs during the impact.
condition: optional/de-activatable automatic door locking system tested per Annex 3 paragraph 1.4.3.5.2.1.

text: Alternatively, the side-door unlocking test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 3, paragraph 1.4.3.5.2.2.
condition: optional/de-activatable automatic door locking system, manufacturer's choice of procedure

text: After the impact, it shall be possible, without the use of tools except those necessary to support the weight of the dummy, to open at least one door per row of seats.
condition: not applicable to convertibles where the top can be easily opened to allow evacuation

text: Where there is no door for a row of seats, it shall be possible after the impact to evacuate all occupants by activating the displacement system of seats, if necessary, without the use of tools.
condition: no door for a row of seats; not applicable to convertibles with easily opened top

text: The door opening / evacuation capability shall be assessed for all configurations or the worst-case configuration for the number of doors on each side of the vehicle and for both left-hand drive and right-hand drive vehicles, when applicable.
condition: when applicable

text: After the impact, it shall be possible without the use of tools to release the dummies from their restraint system, which, if locked, shall be capable of being released by a maximum force of 60 N on the centre of the release control.
After the impact, it shall be possible without the use of tools to remove the dummies from the vehicle without adjustment of the seats.
No more than slight leakage of liquid from the fuel feed installation shall occur on collision.
condition: vehicle propelled by liquid fuel

text: If there is continuous leakage of liquid from the fuel-feed installation after the collision, the rate of leakage shall not exceed 30 g/min.
condition: vehicle propelled by liquid fuel with continuous leakage after collision

text: If the liquid from the fuel-feed system mixes with liquids from other systems and cannot easily be separated and identified, all the liquids collected shall be taken into account in evaluating the continuous leakage.
condition: fuel liquid mixed with other liquids and not easily separable

text: In the case of a compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle, compliance with paragraphs 5.2.7.1. to 5.2.7.3. shall be shown.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The hydrogen leakage rate (VH2) determined according to paragraph 4. of Annex 12 (hydrogen) or paragraph 5. of Annex 12 (helium) shall not exceed an average of 118 NL per minute for the time interval Δt minutes after the crash.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The gas concentration by volume in air in the passenger and luggage compartments, determined according to paragraph 6. of Annex 12, shall not exceed 4.0 per cent for hydrogen or 3.0 per cent for helium at any time throughout the 60 minutes post-crash measurement period.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The concentration requirement is satisfied if it is confirmed that the shut-off valve of each compressed hydrogen storage system has closed within five seconds of first vehicle contact with the barrier and there is no leakage from the compressed hydrogen storage system(s).
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle, alternative compliance route

text: The container(s) for hydrogen storage shall remain attached to the vehicle at a minimum of one attachment point.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Following the Annex 3 test, the electric power train operating on high voltage and the high voltage systems galvanically connected to the high voltage bus of the electric power train shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 5.2.8.1. to 5.2.8.4.
condition: vehicle equipped with high voltage electric power train

text: After the impact, the high voltage buses shall meet at least one of the four criteria of paragraphs 5.2.8.1.1. through 5.2.8.1.4.2.

If the vehicle has an automatic disconnect function or devices that conductively divide the electric power train circuit during driving, at least one of the criteria shall apply to the disconnected circuit or to each divided circuit individually after the disconnect function is activated.
condition: vehicle has automatic disconnect function or circuit-dividing devices

text: The isolation resistance criteria of paragraph 5.2.8.1.4. shall not be applied if more than a single potential of a part of the high voltage bus is not protected under the conditions of protection degree IPXXB.
condition: more than a single potential of the high voltage bus not protected to IPXXB

text: If the crash test is performed with part(s) of the high voltage system not energized, protection against electrical shock for those parts shall be proved by either paragraph 5.2.8.1.3. or paragraph 5.2.8.1.4., except for any coupling system for charging the REESS not energized during driving.
condition: crash test performed with parts of high voltage system not energized
applies_to: coupling system for charging the rechargeable electrical energy storage system

text: Absence of high voltage: the voltages Ub, U1 and U2 of the high voltage buses shall be equal to or less than 30 VAC or 60 VDC within 60 s after the impact when measured according to paragraph 2. of Annex 11.
condition: if absence of high voltage criterion is used

text: Low electrical energy: the Total Energy (TE) on the high voltage buses shall be less than 0.2 joules when measured according to paragraph 3. of Annex 11 with formula (a), or alternatively calculated from measured Ub and manufacturer-specified X-capacitance (Cx) according to formula (b).
condition: if low electrical energy criterion is used

text: The energy stored in the Y-capacitors (TEy1, TEy2) shall also be less than 0.2 joules, calculated from measured voltages U1 and U2 between the high voltage buses and the electrical chassis and the manufacturer-specified Y-capacitance according to formula (c) of paragraph 3. of Annex 11.
condition: if low electrical energy criterion is used

text: Physical protection: protection degree IPXXB against direct contact with high voltage live parts shall be provided, assessed according to paragraph 4 of Annex 11.
condition: if physical protection criterion is used

text: For protection against indirect contact, the resistance between all exposed conductive parts of electrical protection barriers/enclosures and the electrical chassis shall be lower than 0.1 Ω with a current flow of at least 0.2 A.
condition: if physical protection criterion is used

text: The resistance between any two simultaneously reachable exposed conductive parts of electrical protection barriers/enclosures that are less than 2.5 m from each other shall be less than 0.2 Ω with a current flow of at least 0.2 A.
condition: if physical protection criterion is used

text: In case of doubt or if the galvanic connection is established by means other than welding, resistance measurements shall be made using one of the test procedures in paragraph 4.1. of Annex 11 (requirements are deemed satisfied if the connection is welded).
condition: connection not made by welding or in case of doubt

text: Isolation resistance: the criteria of paragraphs 5.2.8.1.4.1. and 5.2.8.1.4.2. shall be met, with measurement conducted according to paragraph 5. of Annex 11.
condition: if isolation resistance criterion is used

text: If the AC and DC high voltage buses are galvanically isolated from each other, isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall have a minimum value of 100 Ω/V of the working voltage for DC buses.
condition: separate galvanically isolated DC and AC buses

text: If the AC and DC high voltage buses are galvanically isolated from each other, isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall have a minimum value of 500 Ω/V of the working voltage for AC buses.
condition: separate galvanically isolated DC and AC buses

text: If the AC and DC high voltage buses are conductively connected, they shall meet one of: (a) isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and electrical chassis of at least 500 Ω/V of working voltage; (b) at least 100 Ω/V and the AC bus meets the physical protection of paragraph 5.2.8.1.3.; or (c) at least 100 Ω/V and the AC bus meets the absence of high voltage of paragraph 5.2.8.1.1.
condition: combined conductively connected DC and AC buses

text: For aqueous electrolyte REESS, from the impact until 60 minutes after the impact there shall be no electrolyte leakage from the REESS into the passenger compartment.
condition: aqueous electrolyte REESS

text: For aqueous electrolyte REESS, from the impact until 60 minutes after the impact no more than 7 per cent by volume of the REESS electrolyte, with a maximum of 5.0 l, shall leak from the REESS to the outside of the passenger compartment.
condition: aqueous electrolyte REESS

text: For collection containers containing Stoddard, coloured coolant and electrolyte, the fluids shall be allowed to separate by specific gravity and then measured.
condition: aqueous electrolyte REESS

text: For non-aqueous electrolyte REESS, from the impact until 60 minutes after the impact there shall be no liquid electrolyte leakage from the REESS into the passenger compartment or luggage compartment and no liquid electrolyte leakage to outside the vehicle.
condition: non-aqueous electrolyte REESS

text: The non-aqueous electrolyte leakage requirement shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the vehicle.
condition: non-aqueous electrolyte REESS

text: The REESS shall remain attached to the vehicle by at least one component anchorage, bracket, or any structure that transfers loads from the REESS to the vehicle structure.
A REESS located outside the passenger compartment shall not enter the passenger compartment.
condition: REESS located outside the passenger compartment

text: From the impact until 60 minutes after the impact, there shall be no evidence of fire or explosion from the REESS.

M1 vehicles of total permissible mass exceeding 2,500 kg based on N1 vehicle types exceeding 2,500 kg are deemed to meet paragraph 5 only where UN Regulation No. 137 is fully complied with and either the angle α between the horizontal plane through the front axle centre and the plane through the front axle centre and the driver's R-point is more than 22°, or the ratio (L101-L114)/L114 is more than 1.30.
condition: M1 > 2,500 kg derived from N1 > 2,500 kg

text: Fulfilment of the conditions of paragraph 5.3.1 shall be verified by the Technical Service, subject to the decision of the Type Approval Authority, and stated under point 8.2. of the approval communication of Annex 1.
condition: paragraph 5.3.1 applied

text: N1 vehicles of total permissible mass exceeding 2,250 kg but not exceeding 2,500 kg are deemed to meet paragraph 5 only where their structural basis is a ladder frame, UN Regulation No. 137 is fully complied with, and either the angle α is more than 22° or the ratio (L101-L114)/L114 is more than 1.30.

Fulfilment of the conditions of paragraph 5.3.2 shall be verified by the Technical Service, subject to the decision of the Type Approval Authority, and stated under point 8.2. of the approval communication of Annex 1.
condition: paragraph 5.3.2 applied

text: For a vehicle fitted with airbag assemblies protecting the driver and other occupants, compliance with paragraphs 8.1.8. to 8.1.9. of UN Regulation No. 16 as amended by the 08 series of amendments shall be demonstrated as from 1 September 2020 for new vehicle types.
condition: vehicle fitted with airbag assemblies; new vehicle types from 1 September 2020

text: Before 1 September 2020, the relevant requirements of the preceding series of amendments of UN Regulation No. 16 apply to airbag user instructions.
condition: before 1 September 2020

text: The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in the Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
Every vehicle approved under this Regulation shall be manufactured so as to conform to the vehicle type approved and satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 5. and 6.
The Type Approval Authority may at any time verify the conformity control methods applied in each production facility; the normal frequency of these verifications shall be once every two years.
The approval mark characters shall have a dimension a of at least 8 mm, as in the model arrangements of Annex 2.
The test area shall be large enough to accommodate the run-up track, barrier and technical installations necessary for the test.
The last part of the track, for at least 5 m before the barrier, shall be horizontal, flat and smooth.
The front face of the barrier consists of a deformable structure as defined in Annex 9.
The front face of the deformable structure is perpendicular within ±1° to the direction of travel of the test vehicle.
The barrier is secured to a mass of not less than 7 x 10^4 kg, the front face of which is vertical within ±1°.
The barrier mass is anchored in the ground or placed on the ground with, if necessary, additional arresting devices to restrict its movement.
The orientation of the barrier is such that the first contact of the vehicle with the barrier is on the steering-column side.

Where there is a choice between carrying out the test with a right-hand or left-hand drive vehicle, the test shall be carried out with the less favourable hand of drive as determined by the Technical Service responsible for the tests.
condition: where there is a choice between right-hand and left-hand drive vehicle

text: The vehicle shall overlap the barrier face by 40 per cent ± 20 mm.
The test vehicle shall be representative of the series production, shall include all the equipment normally fitted and shall be in normal running order.
Some components of the test vehicle may be replaced by equivalent masses only where this substitution clearly has no noticeable effect on the results measured under paragraph 6.
condition: if components are replaced by equivalent masses

text: By agreement between manufacturer and Technical Service the fuel system may be modified so that an appropriate amount of fuel can be used to run the engine or the electrical energy conversion system.
condition: by agreement between manufacturer and Technical Service

text: For the test, the mass of the vehicle submitted shall be the unladen kerb mass.
The fuel tank shall be filled with water to mass equal to 90 per cent of the mass of a full load of fuel as specified by the manufacturer with a tolerance of ±1 per cent.
condition: not applicable to hydrogen fuel tanks

text: All the other systems (brake, cooling, ...) may be empty, in which case the mass of the liquids shall be carefully compensated.
condition: if other systems are empty

text: If the mass of the measuring apparatus on board the vehicle exceeds the 25 kg allowed, it may be compensated by reductions which have no noticeable effect on the results measured under paragraph 6.
condition: if the mass of on-board measuring apparatus exceeds 25 kg

text: The mass of the measuring apparatus shall not change each axle reference load by more than 5 per cent, each variation not exceeding 20 kg.
The mass of the vehicle resulting from the provisions of paragraph 1.4.2.1 shall be indicated in the report.

The steering wheel, if adjustable, shall be placed in the normal position indicated by the manufacturer or, in the absence of any particular recommendation by the manufacturer, midway between the limits of its range(s) of adjustment.
condition: if the steering wheel is adjustable

text: At the end of propelled travel, the steering wheel shall be left free, with its spokes in the position which according to the manufacturer corresponds to straight-ahead travel of the vehicle.

The movable glazing of the vehicle shall be in the closed position; for test measurement purposes and in agreement with the manufacturer, it may be lowered, provided that the position of the operating handle corresponds to the closed position.
The gear-change lever shall be in the neutral position.
condition: unless the vehicle is propelled by its own engine

text: If the vehicle is propelled by its own engine, the gear-change lever position shall be defined by the manufacturer.
condition: if the vehicle is propelled by its own engine

text: The pedals shall be in their normal position of rest.
Adjustable pedals shall be set in their mid-position unless another position is specified by the manufacturer.
condition: if the pedals are adjustable

text: The doors shall be closed but not locked.

The automatically activated door locking system shall be activated at the start of propulsion of the vehicle in order to lock the doors automatically before the moment of impact; at the choice of the manufacturer, the doors shall be locked manually before the start of propulsion of the vehicle.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with an automatically activated door locking system

text: For vehicles with an automatically activated door locking system that is installed optionally and/or can be de-activated by the driver, one of the two procedures of paragraphs 1.4.3.5.2.1 or 1.4.3.5.2.2 shall be used at the choice of the manufacturer.
condition: if the automatically activated door locking system is installed optionally and/or can be de-activated by the driver

text: Under this procedure, the automatically activated door locking system shall be activated at the start of propulsion of the vehicle in order to lock the doors automatically before the moment of impact; at the choice of the manufacturer, the doors shall be locked manually before the start of propulsion.
condition: if the system is optional and/or de-activatable and the manufacturer chooses this procedure

text: Under this procedure, the side doors on the impacted side shall be unlocked and the automatically activated door locking system overridden for these doors.
condition: if the system is optional and/or de-activatable and the manufacturer chooses this procedure

text: Under this procedure, for the side doors on the non-impacted side, the system may be activated to lock these doors automatically before the moment of impact; at the choice of the manufacturer, these doors shall be locked manually before the start of propulsion of the vehicle.
condition: if the system is optional and/or de-activatable and the manufacturer chooses this procedure

text: If an opening or removable roof is fitted, it shall be in place and in the closed position; for test measurement purposes and in agreement with the manufacturer, it may be open.
condition: if an opening or removable roof is fitted

text: The sun-visors shall be in the stowed position.
The interior rear-view mirror shall be in the normal position of use.
Arm-rests at the front and rear, if movable, shall be in the lowered position, unless this is prevented by the position of the dummies in the vehicle.
condition: if arm-rests are movable

text: Head restraints adjustable for height shall be in their appropriate position as defined by the manufacturer.
condition: if head restraints are adjustable for height

text: In the absence of any particular recommendation from the manufacturer, height-adjustable head restraints shall be in their uppermost position.
condition: if no manufacturer recommendation

text: Longitudinally adjustable front seats shall be placed so that their H point, determined per Annex 6, is in the middle position of travel or in the nearest locking position thereto.
condition: if the front seats are adjustable longitudinally

text: Front seats independently adjustable for height shall be placed at the height position defined by the manufacturer.
condition: if independently adjustable for height

text: In the case of a front bench seat, the seat position reference shall be to the H point of the driver's place.
condition: in the case of a bench seat

text: Adjustable front seat-backs shall be adjusted so that the resulting inclination of the torso of the dummy is as close as possible to that recommended by the manufacturer for normal use or, in the absence of any recommendation, to 25° towards the rear from the vertical.
condition: if the front seat-backs are adjustable

text: Adjustable rear seats or rear bench seats shall be placed in the rearmost position.
condition: if the rear seats are adjustable

text: The adjustment of REESS SOC shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 20 ± 10 °C.
condition: vehicles equipped with electric power train

text: Where different charging procedures are possible, the REESS shall be charged using the procedure which yields the highest SOC.
condition: where different charging procedures are possible

text: For a vehicle with a REESS designed to be externally charged, the REESS shall be charged to the highest SOC in accordance with the procedure specified by the manufacturer for normal operation until the charging process is normally terminated.
condition: REESS designed to be externally charged

text: For a vehicle with a REESS designed to be charged only by an energy source on the vehicle, the REESS shall be charged to the highest SOC achievable with normal operation of the vehicle.
condition: REESS designed to be charged only by an on-vehicle energy source

text: The manufacturer shall advise on the vehicle operation mode to attain the highest SOC for a REESS charged only by an energy source on the vehicle.
condition: REESS designed to be charged only by an on-vehicle energy source

text: When the vehicle is tested, SOC shall be no less than 95 per cent of the SOC according to paragraphs 1.4.4.1.1 and 1.4.4.1.2 for REESS designed to be externally charged.
condition: REESS designed to be externally charged

text: When the vehicle is tested, SOC shall be no less than 90 per cent of the SOC according to paragraphs 1.4.4.1.1 and 1.4.4.1.2 for REESS designed to be charged only by an energy source on the vehicle.
condition: REESS designed to be charged only by an on-vehicle energy source

text: SOC will be confirmed by a method provided by the manufacturer.
The electric power train shall be energized with or without the operation of the original electrical energy sources (e.g. engine-generator, REESS or electric energy conversion system).
condition: vehicles equipped with electric power train

text: By agreement between Technical Service and manufacturer the test may be performed with all or parts of the electric power train not being energized insofar as there is no negative influence on the test result.
condition: by agreement between Technical Service and manufacturer

text: For parts of the electric power train not energized, the protection against electrical shock shall be proved by either physical protection or isolation resistance and appropriate additional evidence.
condition: if parts of the electric power train are not energized during the test

text: Where an automatic disconnect is provided, at the request of the manufacturer the test may be performed with the automatic disconnect being triggered.
condition: where an automatic disconnect is provided and at the manufacturer's request

text: If the test is performed with the automatic disconnect triggered, it shall be demonstrated that the automatic disconnect would have operated during the impact test, including the automatic activation signal as well as the galvanic separation considering the conditions as seen during the impact.
condition: if the test is performed with the automatic disconnect triggered

text: A Hybrid III fiftieth percentile male dummy fitted with a 45° ankle and meeting the specifications for its adjustment shall be installed in each of the front outboard seats in accordance with the conditions set out in Annex 5.
The ankle of the dummy shall be certified in accordance with the procedures in Annex 10.
The car will be tested with restraint systems, as provided by the manufacturer.
The vehicle shall be propelled either by its own engine or by any other propelling device.
At the moment of impact the vehicle shall no longer be subject to the action of any additional steering or propelling device.
The course of the vehicle shall be such that it satisfies the requirements of paragraphs 1.2 and 1.3.1 of Annex 3.
Vehicle speed at the moment of impact shall be 56 -0/+1 km/h; if the test was performed at a higher impact speed and the vehicle met the requirements, the test shall be considered satisfactory.
All the measurements necessary for the verification of the performance criteria shall be made with measurement systems corresponding to the specifications of Annex 8.
The different dummy parameters shall be recorded through independent data channels of the specified CFC.
The head acceleration (a) referring to the centre of gravity is calculated from the triaxial components of the acceleration measured with a CFC of 1,000.
The axial tensile force and the fore/aft shear force at the neck/head interface are measured with a CFC of 1,000.
The bending moment about a lateral axis at the neck/head interface is measured with a CFC of 600.
The chest deflection between the sternum and the spine is measured with a CFC of 180.
The femur and tibia axial compressive force and the bending moments are measured with a CFC of 600.
The displacement of the tibia with respect to the femur is measured at the knee sliding joint with a CFC of 180.

The deceleration time history of the structure shall be determined on the basis of the value of the longitudinal accelerometers at the base of the B pillar on the struck side of the vehicle with a CFC of 180 by means of data channels corresponding to the requirements of Annex 8.
condition: to enable the simplified test of Annex 7

text: The speed time history used in the Annex 7 test procedure shall be obtained from the longitudinal accelerometer at the B pillar on the struck side.
The Head Performance Criterion (HPC36) is considered satisfied when, during the test, there is no contact between the head and any vehicle component.
condition: no head contact

text: If, during the test, there is contact between the head and any vehicle component, HPC shall be calculated on the basis of the resultant acceleration (a) measured according to paragraph 5.2.1 of Annex 3, in units of g (1 g = 9,81 m/s2).
condition: if there is head contact

text: If the beginning of the head contact can be determined satisfactorily, t1 and t2 define an interval between the beginning of the head contact and the end of the recording for which the value of HPC is maximum.
condition: if beginning of head contact can be determined

text: If the beginning of the head contact cannot be determined, t1 and t2 define a time interval between the beginning and the end of the recording for which the value of HPC is maximum.
condition: if beginning of head contact cannot be determined

text: Values of HPC for which the time interval (t1 - t2) is greater than 36 ms are ignored for the purposes of calculating the maximum value.

The value of the resultant head acceleration during forward impact which is exceeded for 3 ms cumulatively is calculated from the resultant head acceleration measured according to paragraph 5.2.1 of Annex 3.

The neck injury criteria are determined by the compressive axial force, the axial tensile force and the fore/aft shear forces at the head/neck interface, expressed in kN and measured according to paragraph 5.2.2 of Annex 3, and by the duration of these forces expressed in ms.
The neck bending moment criterion is determined by the bending moment, in Nm, about a lateral axis at the head/neck interface measured according to paragraph 5.2.2 of Annex 3.
The neck flexion bending moment, expressed in Nm, shall be recorded.
The thorax compression criterion is determined by the absolute value of the thorax deformation, in mm, measured according to paragraph 5.2.3 of Annex 3.

The Viscous Criterion (V * C) is calculated as the instantaneous product of the compression and the rate of deflection of the sternum, measured according to paragraph 6 of Annex 4 and paragraph 5.2.3 of Annex 3.

The Femur Force Criterion is determined by the compression load in kN transmitted axially on each femur of the dummy, measured according to paragraph 5.2.4 of Annex 3, and by the duration of the compressive load in ms.
The tibia compressive force criterion is determined by the compressive load (Fz) in kN transmitted axially on each tibia of the dummy, measured according to paragraph 5.2.4 of Annex 3.
For the tibia index calculation, the critical bending moment (MC)R shall be taken to be 225 Nm and the critical compressive force (FC)Z shall be taken to be 35.9 kN.

The tibia index is calculated for the top and the bottom of each tibia; Fz may be measured at either location and used for both calculations, while moments Mx and My are measured separately at both locations.
The viscous criterion is calculated as the instantaneous product of the compression and the rate of deflection of the sternum, both derived from the measurement of sternum deflection.
The sternum deflection response is filtered once at CFC 180 and compression and deflection velocity are calculated from this filtered signal.
The maximum value of the time interval ∂t between the measurements of sternum deflection shall be 1.25 x 10-4 seconds.
For separate seats, the plane of symmetry of the dummy shall coincide with the vertical median plane of the seat.
condition: separate seats

text: On a front bench seat, the plane of symmetry of the driver dummy shall lie in the vertical plane passing through the steering wheel centre and parallel to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
condition: front bench seat

text: If the driver seating position is determined by the shape of the bench, such seat shall be regarded as a separate seat.
condition: if the seating position is determined by the shape of the bench

text: On a front bench seat, the plane of symmetry of the outer passenger dummy shall be symmetrical with that of the driver dummy relative to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
condition: front bench seat

text: If the outer passenger seating position is determined by the shape of the bench, such seat shall be regarded as a separate seat.
condition: if the seating position is determined by the shape of the bench

text: For a bench seat for front passengers (not including driver), the planes of symmetry of the dummy shall coincide with the median planes of the seating positions defined by the manufacturer.
condition: bench seat for front passengers not including driver

text: The transverse instrumentation platform of the head of the test dummy shall be horizontal within 2.5°.

To level the head of the test dummy, the position of the H point shall first be adjusted within the limits of Annex 5 paragraph 2.4.3.1; if still not level, the pelvic angle shall be adjusted within the limits of paragraph 2.4.3.2; if still not level, the neck bracket shall be adjusted the minimum amount necessary to ensure the transverse instrumentation platform of the head is horizontal within 2.5°.
condition: in vehicles with upright seats with non-adjustable backs

text: The driver dummy's upper arms shall be adjacent to the torso with the centrelines as close to a vertical plane as possible.
The passenger dummy's upper arms shall be in contact with the seat back and the sides of the torso.
The palms of the driver test dummy shall be in contact with the outer part of the steering wheel rim at the rim's horizontal centreline.

The thumbs of the driver test dummy shall be over the steering wheel rim and lightly taped to it so that if the hand is pushed upward by a force of not less than 9 N and not more than 22 N, the tape releases the hand from the steering wheel rim.
The palms of the passenger test dummy shall be in contact with the outside of the thigh.
The little finger of the passenger test dummy shall be in contact with the seat cushion.
The upper torso of the driver and passenger test dummies shall rest against the seat back.
condition: in vehicles equipped with bench seats

text: The midsagittal plane of the driver dummy shall be vertical, parallel to the vehicle's longitudinal centreline, and pass through the centre of the steering wheel rim.
condition: in vehicles equipped with bench seats

text: The midsagittal plane of the passenger dummy shall be vertical, parallel to the vehicle's longitudinal centreline and at the same distance from the vehicle's longitudinal centreline as the midsagittal plane of the driver dummy.
condition: in vehicles equipped with bench seats

text: The upper torso of the driver and passenger test dummies shall rest against the seat back.
condition: in vehicles equipped with individual seats

text: The midsagittal plane of the driver and the passenger dummy shall be vertical and shall coincide with the longitudinal centreline of the individual seat.
condition: in vehicles equipped with individual seats

text: The H point of the driver and passenger test dummies shall coincide within 13 mm in the vertical dimension and 13 mm in the horizontal dimension with a point 6 mm below the position of the H point determined using the procedure of Annex 6, with the lower leg and thigh segments of the H point machine adjusted to 414 and 401 mm instead of 417 and 432 mm respectively.

The pelvic angle of the dummy, determined using the pelvic angle gauge (GM) drawing 78051-532 inserted into the H point gauging hole, measured from the horizontal on the 76.2 mm (3 inch) flat surface of the gauge, shall be 22.5 degrees plus or minus 2.5 degrees.
The upper legs of the driver and passenger test dummies shall rest against the seat cushion to the extent permitted by placement of the feet.
The initial distance between the outboard knee clevis flange surfaces of the dummies shall be 270 mm ± 10 mm.
To the extent practicable, the left leg of the driver dummy and both legs of the passenger dummy shall be in vertical longitudinal planes.
To the extent practicable, the right leg of the driver dummy shall be in a vertical plane; final adjustment to accommodate placement of feet in accordance with paragraph 2.6 is permitted.
The right foot of the driver test dummy shall rest on the undepressed accelerator with the rearmost point of the heel on the floor surface in the plane of the pedal.

If the right foot of the driver dummy cannot be placed on the accelerator pedal, it shall be positioned perpendicular to the tibia and placed as far forward as possible in the direction of the centreline of the pedal with the rearmost point of the heel resting on the floor surface.
condition: if the foot cannot be placed on the accelerator pedal

text: The heel of the left foot of the driver dummy shall be placed as far forward as possible and shall rest on the floor pan.
The left foot of the driver dummy shall be positioned as flat as possible on the toe board.
The longitudinal centreline of the left foot of the driver dummy shall be placed as parallel as possible to the longitudinal centreline of the vehicle.
At the request of the manufacturer it shall be possible to place the left foot of the driver dummy on the footrest, in which case the position of the left foot is defined by the footrest.
condition: for vehicles equipped with a footrest, at the request of the manufacturer

text: The heels of both feet of the passenger test dummy shall be placed as far forward as possible and shall rest on the floor pan.
Both feet of the passenger test dummy shall be positioned as flat as possible on the toe board.
The longitudinal centreline of the feet of the passenger test dummy shall be placed as parallel as possible to the longitudinal centreline of the vehicle.
The measuring instruments installed shall not in any way affect the movement of the dummy during impact.
The temperature of the dummy and the system of measuring instruments shall be stabilized before the test and maintained so far as possible within a range between 19 °C and 22.2 °C.

The instrumented dummies shall be clothed in formfitting cotton stretch garments with short sleeves and mid-calf length trousers specified in FMVSS 208, drawings 78051-292 and 293 or their equivalent.

A size 11XW shoe meeting the configuration size, sole and heel thickness specifications of US military standard MIL S 13192, revision P, and weighing 0.57 ± 0.1 kg, shall be placed and fastened on each foot of the test dummies.
The dummy jacket shall be installed at the position where the bolt hole of the neck lower bracket and the work hole of the dummy jacket are at the same position.
With the test dummy at its designated seating position, the belt shall be placed around the test dummy, the latch fastened and all slack removed from the lap belt.
The upper torso webbing shall be pulled out of the retractor horizontally at a position via the centre of the dummy and allowed to retract, this operation being repeated four times.
The shoulder belt shall be positioned so that it does not come off the shoulder and does not contact the neck.
For the Hybrid III fiftieth percentile male dummy, the seat belt path shall be positioned so that the hole of the outer side dummy jacket is not fully hidden by the seat belt.
A 9 to 18 N tension load shall be applied to the lap belt.
The maximum amount of slack recommended by the manufacturer for normal use in the owner's manual shall be introduced into the upper torso belt.
condition: if the belt system is equipped with a tension-relieving device

text: The excess webbing in the shoulder belt shall be allowed to be retracted by the rewind force of the retractor.
condition: if the belt system is not equipped with a tension-relieving device

text: The safety belt may be manually adjusted and retained by tape only where the safety belt and its anchorages are located such that the belt does not lie as required.
condition: where the belt does not lie as required

text: The H point and actual torso angle for seating positions shall be determined in accordance with the procedure described in Addendum 6 of Mutual Resolution No. 1 (M.R.1) (document ECE/TRANS/WP.29/1101/Amend.5).
The trolley shall be so constructed that no permanent deformation appears after the test.
condition: simplified trolley test

text: The trolley shall be so guided that, during the impact phase, the deviation does not exceed 5° in the vertical plane and 2° in the horizontal plane.
condition: simplified trolley test

text: The structure tested on the trolley shall be representative of the series production of the vehicles concerned; components may be replaced or removed only where this clearly has no effect on the test results.
condition: simplified trolley test

text: Adjustments of the structure tested on the trolley shall conform to those set out in paragraph 1.4.3 of Annex 3, taking into account paragraph 1.2.1 of Annex 7.
condition: simplified trolley test

text: The structure shall be firmly attached to the trolley in such a way that no relative displacement occurs during the test.
condition: simplified trolley test

text: The method used to fasten the structure to the trolley shall not have the effect of strengthening the seat anchorages or restraint devices, or of producing any abnormal deformation of the structure.
condition: simplified trolley test

text: The recommended attachment device is one whereby the structure rests on supports placed approximately in the axis of the wheels or, if possible, is secured to the trolley by the fastenings of the suspension system.
condition: simplified trolley test

text: The angle between the longitudinal axis of the vehicle and the direction of motion of the trolley shall be 0° ± 2°.
condition: simplified trolley test

text: The dummies and their positioning in the trolley test shall conform to the specifications in Annex 3, paragraph 2.
condition: simplified trolley test

text: The transducers measuring the deceleration of the structure during the impact shall be positioned parallel to the longitudinal axis of the trolley according to the specifications of Annex 8 (CFC 180).
condition: simplified trolley test

text: The measurements on the dummies in the trolley test shall be made as set out in Annex 3, paragraph 5.
condition: simplified trolley test

text: The deceleration curve of the structure during the impact phase shall be such that the variation of speed in relation to time curve obtained by integration at no point differs by more than ±1 m/s from the reference curve of the vehicle concerned as defined in the appendix to Annex 7; a displacement with regard to the time axis of the reference curve may be used.
condition: simplified trolley test

text: The reference curve ΔV = f(t) shall be obtained by integration of the deceleration curve of the vehicle concerned measured in the frontal collision barrier test as provided for in paragraph 6 of Annex 3.
condition: simplified trolley test

text: The simplified test may be performed by a method other than deceleration of a trolley only provided that the method complies with the requirement concerning the range of variation of speed in paragraph 1.6 of Annex 7.
condition: if an equivalent method is used

text: The absolute value of the linearity error of a data channel at any frequency in the CFC shall be equal to or less than 2.5 per cent of the value of the CAC, over the whole measurement range.
The frequency response of a data channel shall lie within the limiting curves given in Figure 1 of Annex 8, the zero dB line being determined by the calibration factor.
The phase delay time between the input and output signals of a data channel shall be determined and shall not vary by more than 1/10 FH seconds between 0.03 FH and FH.
A time base shall be recorded and shall at least give 1/100 s with an accuracy of 1 per cent.

The relative time delay between the signals of two or more data channels, regardless of their frequency class, shall not exceed 1 ms excluding delay caused by phase shift; this applies to analogue signals, synchronization pulses and digital signals.
Two or more data channels whose signals are combined shall have the same frequency class and shall not have a relative time delay greater than 1/10 FH seconds.
condition: if signals of data channels are combined

text: The transducer cross sensitivity shall be less than 5 per cent in any direction.
A data channel shall be calibrated at least once a year against reference equipment traceable to known standards.
The methods used to carry out a comparison with reference equipment shall not introduce an error greater than 1 per cent of the CAC.
The use of the reference equipment shall be limited to the frequency range for which it has been calibrated.
The accuracy of the reference equipment for calibration shall be certified or endorsed by an official metrology service.
In static calibration of accelerations, the errors of the reference equipment shall be less than ±1.5 per cent of the channel amplitude class.
In static calibration of forces, the error of the reference equipment shall be less than ±1 per cent of the channel amplitude class.
In static calibration of displacements, the error of the reference equipment shall be less than ±1 per cent of the channel amplitude class.
In dynamic calibration, the error in the reference accelerations shall be less than ±1.5 per cent of the channel amplitude class below 400 Hz.
In dynamic calibration, the error in the reference accelerations shall be less than ±2 per cent of the channel amplitude class between 400 Hz and 900 Hz.
In dynamic calibration, the error in the reference accelerations shall be less than ±2.5 per cent of the channel amplitude class above 900 Hz.
The relative error in the reference time shall be less than 10-5.
The sensitivity coefficient and the linearity error shall be determined by measuring the output signal of the data channel against a known input signal for various values of this signal.
The calibration of the data channel shall cover the whole range of the amplitude class.
For bi-directional channels, both the positive and negative values shall be used in calibration.
condition: for bi-directional channels

text: If the calibration equipment cannot produce the required input owing to excessively high values, calibrations shall be carried out within the limits of the calibration standards and these limits shall be recorded in the test report.
condition: if the calibration equipment cannot produce the required input

text: A total data channel shall be calibrated at a frequency or at a spectrum of frequencies having a significant value within the specified range.

The response curves of phase and amplitude against frequency shall be determined by measuring the output signals of the data channel against a known input signal for various values varying between FL and 10 times the CFC or 3,000 Hz, whichever is lower.
A regular check shall be made to identify any environmental influence (such as electric or magnetic flux, cable velocity, etc.) on the data channels.
If significant output signals due to environmental influence are obtained, corrective action shall be taken, for instance by replacement of cables.
condition: if significant output signals are obtained

text: The CAC of a data channel shall be 1, 2 or 5 to a power of ten.

Transducers should be rigidly secured so that their recordings are affected by vibration as little as possible; any mounting having a lowest resonance frequency equal to at least 5 times the frequency FH of the data channel considered shall be considered valid.
Acceleration transducers should be mounted in such a way that the initial angle of the real measurement axis to the corresponding axis of the reference axis system is not greater than 5°.
condition: unless an analytical or experimental assessment of the effect of the mounting on the collected data is made

text: Each acceleration transducer axis should pass within 10 mm of the point at which multi-axial accelerations are to be measured.
condition: when multi-axial accelerations at a point are to be measured

text: The centre of seismic mass of each accelerometer should be within 30 mm of the point at which multi-axial accelerations are to be measured.
condition: when multi-axial accelerations at a point are to be measured

text: Filtering corresponding to the frequencies of the data channel class may be carried out during either recording or processing of data.

Before recording, analogical filtering at a higher level than CFC should be effected in order to use at least 50 per cent of the dynamic range of the recorder and to reduce the risk of high frequencies saturating the recorder or causing aliasing errors in the digitalizing process.
The sampling frequency should be equal to at least 8 FH.
The sampling frequency can be divided by the speed ratio.
condition: in the case of analogical recording, when the recording and reading speeds are different

text: The size of digital words should be at least 7 bits and a parity bit.
The results should be presented on A4 size paper (ISO/R 216).
Results presented as diagrams should have axes scaled with a measurement unit corresponding to a suitable multiple of the chosen unit (for example, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 millimetres).
condition: if results are presented as diagrams

text: SI units shall be used for the presentation of results, except that km/h may be used for vehicle velocity and g, with g = 9.8 m/s2, may be used for accelerations due to impact.

The main honeycomb block of the deformable barrier shall have a height of 650 mm (in direction of honeycomb ribbon axis), a width of 1,000 mm and a depth of 450 mm (in direction of honeycomb cell axes), with a tolerance of ±2.5 mm.
The main honeycomb block of the deformable barrier shall be of Aluminium 3003 (ISO 209, Part 1).
The main honeycomb block shall have a foil thickness of 0.076 mm ± 15 per cent.
The main honeycomb block shall have a cell size of 19.1 mm ± 20 per cent.
The main honeycomb block shall have a density of 28.6 kg/m3 ± 20 per cent.
The main honeycomb block shall have a crush strength of 0.342 MPa + 0 per cent -10 per cent, in accordance with the certification procedure described in paragraph 2. of Annex 9.

The bumper element of the deformable barrier shall have a height of 330 mm (in direction of honeycomb ribbon axis), a width of 1,000 mm and a depth of 90 mm (in direction of honeycomb cell axes), with a tolerance of ±2.5 mm.
The bumper element of the deformable barrier shall be of Aluminium 3003 (ISO 209, Part 1).
The bumper element shall have a foil thickness of 0.076 mm ± 15 per cent.
The bumper element shall have a cell size of 6.4 mm ± 20 per cent.
The bumper element shall have a density of 82.6 kg/m3 ± 20 per cent.
The bumper element shall have a crush strength of 1.711 MPa +0 per cent -10 per cent, in accordance with the certification procedure described in paragraph 2. of Annex 9.
The backing sheet of the deformable barrier shall have a height of 800 mm ± 2.5 mm.
The backing sheet of the deformable barrier shall have a width of 1,000 mm ± 2.5 mm.
The backing sheet of the deformable barrier shall have a thickness of 2.0 mm ± 0.1 mm.
The cladding sheet of the deformable barrier shall have a length of 1,700 mm ± 2.5 mm.
The cladding sheet of the deformable barrier shall have a width of 1,000 mm ± 2.5 mm.
The cladding sheet of the deformable barrier shall have a thickness of 0.81 ± 0.07 mm.
The cladding sheet of the deformable barrier shall be of Aluminium 5251/5052 (ISO 209, part 1).
The bumper facing sheet of the deformable barrier shall have a height of 330 mm ± 2.5 mm.
The bumper facing sheet of the deformable barrier shall have a width of 1,000 mm ± 2.5 mm.
The bumper facing sheet of the deformable barrier shall have a thickness of 0.81 mm ± 0.07 mm.
The bumper facing sheet of the deformable barrier shall be of Aluminium 5251/5052 (ISO 209, part 1).
The adhesive used throughout the deformable barrier should be a two-part polyurethane (such as Ciba-Geigy XB5090/1 resin with XB5304 hardener, or equivalent).

The aluminium honeycomb certification procedure summarised in Annex 9 (based on NHTSA TP-214D) should be applied to the materials for the frontal impact barrier having a crush strength of 0.342 MPa and 1.711 MPa respectively.
Eight honeycomb samples shall be taken from four locations evenly spaced across the honeycomb block to ensure uniformity of crush strength across the whole of the barrier face.
For a honeycomb block to pass certification, seven of the eight samples shall meet the crush strength requirements.
Four samples, each measuring 300 mm x 300 mm x 50 mm thick, shall be cut from the block of barrier face material, located as illustrated in Figure 2 of Annex 9.
Each of the 300 mm x 300 mm x 50 mm samples shall be cut into samples for certification testing of 150 mm x 150 mm x 50 mm.
Honeycomb certification shall be based on the testing of two samples from each of the four locations; the other two should be made available to the applicant upon request.
Honeycomb test samples shall have a length of 150 mm ± 6 mm, a width of 150 mm ± 6 mm and a thickness of 50 mm ± 2 mm.
The walls of incomplete cells around the edge of the honeycomb sample shall be trimmed so that in the "W" direction the fringes are no greater than 1.8 mm.
In the "L" direction, half the length of one bonded cell wall (in the ribbon direction) shall be left at either end of the honeycomb specimen.
The length of the honeycomb sample shall be measured in three locations, 12.7 mm from each end and in the middle, and recorded as L1, L2 and L3.
The width of the honeycomb sample shall be measured in the same manner and recorded as W1, W2 and W3.
The length and width measurements of the honeycomb sample shall be taken on the centreline of the thickness, and the crush area shall then be calculated from them.
The honeycomb sample shall be crushed at a rate of not less than 5.1 mm/min and not more than 7.6 mm/min.
The minimum crush distance of the honeycomb sample shall be 16.5 mm.
Force versus deflection data are to be collected in either analog or digital form for each honeycomb sample tested.
A means of converting analog force versus deflection data to digital shall be available.
condition: if analog data are collected

text: All digital force versus deflection data shall be collected at a rate of not less than 5 Hz (5 points per second).
For crush strength determination, all data prior to 6.4 mm of crush and after 16.5 mm of crush shall be ignored.

The remaining crush data shall be divided into three displacement intervals: (1) 06.4 mm - 09.7 mm inclusive, (2) 09.7 mm - 13.2 mm exclusive, (3) 13.2 mm - 16.5 mm inclusive, and the average force and crush strength of each section shall be calculated.
For a honeycomb sample of 0.342 MPa material to pass certification, the crush strength of each section shall satisfy 0.308 MPa ≤ S(n) ≤ 0.342 MPa, for n = 1, 2, 3.
condition: for 0.342 MPa material

text: For a honeycomb sample of 1.711 MPa material to pass certification, the crush strength of each section shall satisfy 1.540 MPa ≤ S(n) ≤ 1.711 MPa, for n = 1, 2, 3.
condition: for 1.711 MPa material

text: Eight honeycomb samples are to be tested from four locations evenly spaced across the block, and for a block to pass certification seven of the eight samples shall meet the sample crush strength specification.

Immediately before bonding, aluminium sheet surfaces to be bonded shall be thoroughly cleaned using a suitable solvent, such as 1-1-1 Trichloroethane, at least twice or as required to eliminate grease or dirt deposits.
The cleaned aluminium surfaces shall then be thoroughly abraded using 120 grit abrasive paper, changing the abrasive paper regularly during the process to avoid clogging.
Metallic/Silicon Carbide abrasive paper is not to be used for abrading the aluminium surfaces.
Following abrading, the aluminium surfaces shall be thoroughly cleaned again with solvent, so that in total the surfaces are solvent cleaned at least four times.
All dust and deposits left as a result of the abrading process shall be removed before bonding.
The adhesive should be applied to one surface only, using a ribbed rubber roller.
The adhesive should be applied to the aluminium sheet only.
condition: where honeycomb is to be bonded to aluminium sheet

text: A maximum of 0.5 kg/m2 of adhesive shall be applied evenly over the surface, giving a maximum film thickness of 0.5 mm.
The main honeycomb block shall be bonded to the backing sheet with adhesive such that the cell axes are perpendicular to the sheet.
The cladding shall be bonded to the front surface of the main honeycomb block.
The top and bottom surfaces of the cladding sheet shall not be bonded to the main honeycomb block but should be positioned closely to it.
The cladding sheet shall be adhesively bonded to the backing sheet at the mounting flanges.
The bumper element shall be adhesively bonded to the front of the cladding sheet such that the cell axes are perpendicular to the sheet.
The bottom of the bumper element shall be flush with the bottom surface of the cladding sheet.
The bumper facing sheet shall be adhesively bonded to the front of the bumper element.
The bumper element shall be divided into three equal sections by means of two horizontal slots cut through the entire depth of the bumper section and extending the whole width of the bumper.
The bumper element slots shall be cut using a saw; their width shall be the width of the blade used and shall not exceed 4.0 mm.
Clearance holes for mounting the barrier are to be drilled in the mounting flanges and shall be of 9.5 mm diameter.
Five mounting holes shall be drilled in the top flange at a distance of 40 mm from the top edge of the flange and five in the bottom flange, 40 mm from the bottom edge of that flange.
condition: unless alternative positions offering at least the same mounting strength and security are used

text: The mounting holes shall be at 100 mm, 300 mm, 500 mm, 700 mm, 900 mm from either edge of the barrier, drilled to ±1 mm of the nominal distances.
condition: unless alternative positions offering at least the same mounting strength and security are used

text: Alternative mounting hole positions may be used only if they offer at least the mounting strength and security provided by the specified mounting specifications.
condition: if alternative hole positions are used

text: The deformable barrier shall be rigidly fixed to the edge of a mass of not less than 7 x 104 kg or to some structure attached thereto.

The attachment of the barrier face shall be such that the vehicle shall not contact any part of the structure more than 75 mm from the top surface of the barrier (excluding the upper flange) during any stage of the impact.
The front face of the surface to which the deformable barrier is attached shall be flat and continuous over the height and width of the face.
The front face of the surface to which the deformable barrier is attached shall be vertical ±1° and perpendicular ±1° to the axis of the run-up track.
The barrier attachment surface shall not be displaced by more than 10 mm during the test.
Additional anchorage or arresting devices shall be used to prevent displacement of the concrete block.
condition: if necessary

text: The edge of the deformable barrier shall be aligned with the edge of the concrete block appropriate for the side of the vehicle to be tested.
The deformable barrier shall be fixed to the concrete block by means of ten bolts, five in the top mounting flange and five in the bottom, of at least 8 mm diameter.
Steel clamping strips shall be used for both the top and bottom mounting flanges of the deformable barrier.
The steel clamping strips shall be 60 mm high and 1,000 mm wide and have a thickness of at least 3 mm.
The edges of the clamping strips should be rounded-off to prevent tearing of the barrier against the strip during impact.
The edge of the clamping strip should be located no more than 5 mm above the base of the upper barrier-mounting flange, or 5 mm below the top of the lower barrier-mounting flange.
Five clearance holes of 9.5 mm diameter must be drilled in both clamping strips to correspond with those in the mounting flange on the barrier.

The mounting strip and barrier flange holes may be widened from 9.5 mm up to a maximum of 25 mm in order to accommodate differences in back-plate arrangements and/or Load Cell Wall hole configurations.
None of the barrier mounting fixtures shall fail in the impact test.

Where a load cell wall is present, the mounting strips may be extended to accommodate higher mounting holes for the bolts; if extended, thicker gauge steel should be used such that the barrier does not pull away from the wall, bend or tear during the impact.
condition: where the deformable barrier is mounted on a load cell wall (LCW)

text: An alternative method of mounting the barrier should be at least as secure as that specified in Annex 9 paragraphs 5.1 and 5.2.
condition: if an alternative method of mounting the barrier is used

text: For the upper foot impact test, the complete Hybrid III lower leg assembly, left (86-5001-001) and right (86-5001-002), equipped with the foot and ankle assembly, left (78051-614) and right (78051-615), shall be used, including the knee assembly.
For the upper foot impact test, the load cell simulator (78051-319 Rev A) shall be used to secure the knee assembly (79051-16 Rev B) to the test fixture.
For the upper foot impact test, each leg assembly shall be soaked for four hours prior to the test at a temperature of 22 °C ± 3 °C and a relative humidity of 40 ± 30 per cent.
The soak period of the leg assembly shall not include the time required to reach steady state conditions.
Prior to the upper foot impact test, the impact surface of the skin and the impactor face shall be cleaned with isopropyl alcohol or equivalent and dusted with talc.
For the upper foot impact test, the impactor accelerometer shall be aligned with its sensitive axis parallel to the direction of impact at contact with the foot.
For the upper foot impact test, the leg assembly shall be mounted to the fixture shown in Figure 1 of Annex 10, and the test fixture shall be rigidly secured to prevent movement during impact.
For the upper foot impact test, the centre line of the femur load cell simulator (78051-319) shall be vertical with a tolerance of ±0.5°.

For the upper foot impact test, the mount shall be adjusted such that the line joining the knee clevis joint and the ankle attachment bolt is horizontal with a tolerance of ±3°, with the heel resting on two sheets of a flat low friction (PTFE sheet) surface.
For the upper foot impact test, the tibia flesh shall be located fully towards the knee end of the tibia.

For the upper foot impact test, the ankle shall be adjusted such that the plane of the underside of the foot is vertical and perpendicular to the direction of impact with a tolerance of ±3° and such that the mid sagittal plane of the foot is aligned with the pendulum arm.
For the upper foot impact test, the knee joint shall be adjusted to 1.5 ± 0.5 g range before each test.
For the upper foot impact test, the ankle joint shall be adjusted so that it is free and then tightened just sufficiently to keep the foot stable on the PTFE sheet.
The rigid impactor for the upper foot impact test shall comprise a horizontal cylinder of diameter 50 ± 2 mm and a pendulum support arm of diameter 19 ± 1 mm.
The impactor cylinder shall have a mass of 1.25 ± 0.02 kg including instrumentation and any part of the support arm within the cylinder.
The impactor pendulum arm shall have a mass of 285 ± 5 g.
The mass of any rotating part of the axle to which the impactor support arm is attached should not be greater than 100 g.
The length between the central horizontal axis of the impactor cylinder and the axis of rotation of the whole pendulum shall be 1,250 ± 1 mm.
The impact cylinder shall be mounted with its longitudinal axis horizontal and perpendicular to the direction of impact.

In the upper foot impact test the pendulum shall impact the underside of the foot at a distance of 185 ± 2 mm from the base of the heel resting on the rigid horizontal platform, so that the longitudinal centre line of the pendulum arm falls within 1° of a vertical line at impact.
The impactor shall be guided to exclude significant lateral, vertical or rotational movement.
A period of at least 30 minutes shall be allowed between successive upper foot impact tests on the same leg.
The data acquisition system for the upper foot impact test, including transducers, shall conform to the specifications for CFC 600, as described in Annex 8.
When each ball of the foot is impacted at 6.7 (±0.1) m/s in accordance with paragraph 1.3. of Annex 10, the maximum lower tibia bending moment about the y-axis (My) shall be 120 ± 25 Nm.

For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the complete Hybrid III lower leg assembly, left (86-5001-001) and right (86-5001-002), equipped with the foot and ankle assembly, left (78051-614) and right (78051-615), shall be used, including the knee assembly.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the load cell simulator (78051-319 Rev A) shall be used to secure the knee assembly (79051-16 Rev B) to the test fixture.

For the lower foot impact test without shoe, each leg assembly shall be soaked for four hours prior to the test at a temperature of 22 ± 3 °C and a relative humidity of 40 ± 30 per cent; the soak period shall not include the time required to reach steady state conditions.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the impact surface of the skin and the impactor face shall be cleaned with isopropyl alcohol or equivalent prior to the test and dusted with talc.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, it shall be checked that there is no visible damage to the energy absorbing insert to the heel.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the impactor accelerometer shall be aligned with its sensitive axis parallel to the impactor longitudinal centre line.

For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the leg assembly shall be mounted to the fixture shown in Figure 2 of Annex 10, and the test fixture shall be rigidly secured to prevent movement during impact.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the centre line of the femur load cell simulator (78051-319) shall be vertical with a tolerance of ±0.5°.

For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the mount shall be adjusted such that the line joining the knee clevis joint and the ankle attachment bolt is horizontal with a tolerance of ±3°, with the heel resting on two sheets of a flat low friction (PTFE sheet) surface.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the tibia flesh shall be located fully towards the knee end of the tibia.

For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the ankle shall be adjusted such that the plane of the underside of the foot is vertical and perpendicular to the direction of the impact with a tolerance of ±3° and such that the mid sagittal plane of the foot is aligned with the pendulum arm.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the knee joint shall be adjusted to 1.5 ± 0.5 g range before each test.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the ankle joint shall be adjusted so that it is free and then tightened just sufficiently to keep the foot stable on the PTFE sheet.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the rigid impactor shall comprise a horizontal cylinder of diameter 50 ± 2 mm and a pendulum support arm of diameter 19 ± 1 mm.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the impactor cylinder shall have a mass of 1.25 ± 0.02 kg including instrumentation and any part of the support arm within the cylinder.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the pendulum arm shall have a mass of 285 ± 5 g.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the mass of any rotating part of the axle to which the support arm is attached should not be greater than 100 g.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the length between the central horizontal axis of the impactor cylinder and the axis of rotation of the whole pendulum shall be 1,250 ± 1 mm.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the impact cylinder shall be mounted with its longitudinal axis horizontal and perpendicular to the direction of impact.

For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the pendulum shall impact the underside of the foot at a distance of 62 ± 2 mm from the base of the heel resting on the rigid horizontal platform, so that the longitudinal centreline of the pendulum arm falls within 1° of a vertical line at impact.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the impactor shall be guided to exclude significant lateral, vertical or rotational movement.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, a period of at least 30 minutes shall be allowed between successive tests on the same leg.
For the lower foot impact test without shoe, the data acquisition system, including transducers, shall conform to the specifications for CFC 600, as described in Annex 8.
When each heel of the dummy foot is impacted at 4.4 ± 0.1 m/s in accordance with paragraph 2.3. of Annex 10, the maximum impactor acceleration shall be 295 ± 50 g.

For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the complete Hybrid III lower leg assembly, left (86-5001-001) and right (86-5001-002), equipped with the foot and ankle assembly, left (78051-614) and right (78051-615), shall be used, including the knee assembly.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the load cell simulator (78051-319 Rev A) shall be used to secure the knee assembly (79051-16 Rev B) to the test fixture.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the foot shall be fitted with the shoe specified in Annex 5, paragraph 2.9.2.

For the lower foot impact test with shoe, each leg assembly shall be soaked for four hours prior to the test at a temperature of 22 ± 3 °C and a relative humidity of 40 ± 30 per cent; the soak period shall not include the time required to reach steady state conditions.

For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the impact surface of the underside of the shoe shall be cleaned with a clean cloth and the impactor face with isopropyl alcohol or equivalent prior to the test.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, it shall be checked that there is no visible damage to the energy absorbing insert to the heel.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the impactor accelerometer shall be aligned with its sensitive axis parallel to the impactor longitudinal centre line.

For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the leg assembly shall be mounted to the fixture shown in Figure 3 of Annex 10, and the test fixture shall be rigidly secured to prevent movement during impact.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the centre line of the femur load cell simulator (78051-319) shall be vertical with a tolerance of ±0.5°.

For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the mount shall be adjusted such that the line joining the knee clevis joint and the ankle attachment bolt is horizontal with a tolerance of ±3°, with the heel of the shoe resting on two sheets of a flat low friction (PTFE sheet) surface.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the tibia flesh shall be located fully towards the knee end of the tibia.

For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the ankle shall be adjusted such that a plane in contact with the heel and sole of the underside of the shoe is vertical and perpendicular to the direction of impact with a tolerance of ±3° and such that the mid sagittal plane of the foot and shoe is aligned with the pendulum arm.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the knee joint shall be adjusted to 1.5 ± 0.5 g range before each test.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the ankle joint shall be adjusted so that it is free and then tightened just sufficiently to keep the foot stable on the PTFE sheet.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the rigid impactor shall comprise a horizontal cylinder of diameter 50 ± 2 mm and a pendulum support arm of diameter 19 ± 1 mm.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the impactor cylinder shall have a mass of 1.25 ± 0.02 kg including instrumentation and any part of the support arm within the cylinder.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the pendulum arm shall have a mass of 285 ± 5 g.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the mass of any rotating part of the axle to which the support arm is attached should not be greater than 100 g.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the length between the central horizontal axis of the impactor cylinder and the axis of rotation of the whole pendulum shall be 1,250 ± 1 mm.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the impact cylinder shall be mounted with its longitudinal axis horizontal and perpendicular to the direction of impact.

For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the pendulum shall impact the heel of the shoe in a horizontal plane which is a distance of 62 ± 2 mm above the base of the dummy heel when the shoe is resting on the rigid horizontal platform, so that the longitudinal centreline of the pendulum arm falls within one degree of a vertical line at impact.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the impactor shall be guided to exclude significant lateral, vertical or rotational movement.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, a period of at least 30 minutes shall be allowed between successive tests on the same leg.
For the lower foot impact test with shoe, the data acquisition system, including transducers, shall conform to the specifications for CFC 600, as described in Annex 8.
When the heel of the shoe is impacted at 6.7 ± 0.1 m/s in accordance with paragraph 3.3. of Annex 10, the maximum Tibia compressive force (Fz) shall be 3.3 ± 0.5 kN.
If a high voltage disconnect function is used, measurements are to be taken from both sides of the device performing the disconnect function.
condition: if a high voltage disconnect function is used

text: If the high voltage disconnect is integral to the REESS or the energy conversion system and the high-voltage bus of the REESS or the energy conversion system is protected according to protection degree IPXXB following the impact test, measurements may only be taken between the device performing the disconnect function and the electrical loads.
condition: if the high voltage disconnect is integral to the REESS or energy conversion system and its high-voltage bus is protected to IPXXB after the impact

text: The voltmeter used in the electrical safety tests shall measure DC values and have an internal resistance of at least 10 MΩ.
After the impact test, the high voltage bus voltages (Ub, U1, U2) shall be determined, with the voltage measurement made not earlier than 10 seconds, but not later than 60 seconds after the impact.
condition: if voltage is measured and the electric power train is energized during the test

text: For the low electrical energy assessment, prior to the impact a switch S1 and a known discharge resistor Re shall be connected in parallel to the relevant capacitance.
condition: if the electric power train is energized during the test

text: Not earlier than 10 seconds and not later than 60 seconds after the impact the switch S1 shall be closed while the voltage Ub and the current Ie are measured and recorded; the product of Ub and Ie shall be integrated from the moment S1 is closed (tc) until Ub falls below the high voltage threshold of 60 V DC (th), the resulting integration being the Total Energy (TE) in joules.
condition: if the low electrical energy criterion is assessed by measurement (formula (a)) with the electric power train energized

text: When Ub is measured at a point in time between 10 seconds and 60 seconds after the impact and the capacitance of the X-capacitors (Cx) is specified by the manufacturer, Total Energy (TE) shall be calculated as TE = 0.5 x Cx x Ub².
