condition: if Cx is specified by the manufacturer and the electric power train is energized

text: When U1 and U2 are measured at a point in time between 10 seconds and 60 seconds after the impact and the capacitances of the Y-capacitors (Cy1, Cy2) are specified by the manufacturer, the energies shall be calculated as TEy1 = 0.5 x Cy1 x U1² and TEy2 = 0.5 x Cy2 x U2².
condition: if Cy1 and Cy2 are specified by the manufacturer and the electric power train is energized

text: Following the vehicle impact test, any parts surrounding the high voltage components shall be, without the use of tools, opened, disassembled or removed, and all remaining surrounding parts shall be considered part of the physical protection.
The jointed test finger described in Figure 3 of Annex 11 shall be inserted into any gaps or openings of the physical protection with a test force of 10 N ± 10 per cent.

If partial or full penetration into the physical protection by the jointed test finger occurs, starting from the straight position both joints of the test finger shall be rotated progressively through an angle of up to 90 degrees with respect to the axis of the adjoining section of the finger and shall be placed in every possible position.
condition: if partial or full penetration by the jointed test finger occurs

text: If appropriate, a low-voltage supply of not less than 40 V and not more than 50 V in series with a suitable lamp should be connected between the jointed test finger and high voltage live parts inside the electrical protection barrier or enclosure.
condition: if appropriate

text: The jointed test finger shall be of metal, except where otherwise specified, with tolerances on dimensions without specific tolerance of +0/-10 seconds on angles, +0/-0.05 mm on linear dimensions up to 25 mm and ±0.2 mm on linear dimensions over 25 mm.
Both joints of the jointed test finger shall permit movement in the same plane and the same direction through an angle of 90° with a 0 to +10° tolerance.
The physical protection requirements of paragraph 5.2.8.1.3. are met only if the jointed test finger is unable to contact high voltage live parts.
If the physical protection requirement is verified by a signal circuit between the jointed test finger and high voltage live parts, the lamp shall not light.
condition: if verified by a signal circuit

text: When measuring electric resistance with a resistance tester, the resistance tester shall have a measurement current of at least 0.2 A and a resolution of 0.01 Ω or less.
condition: if the resistance tester method is used

text: The resistance R measured with the resistance tester between the electrical chassis and the electro conductive enclosure/electrical protection barrier shall be less than 0.1 Ω.
condition: if the resistance tester method is used

text: When measuring electric resistance with a DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter, the voltage of the DC power supply shall be adjusted so that the current flow becomes at least 0.2 A, and R shall be calculated as R = U / I.
condition: if the DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter method is used

text: The resistance R calculated with the DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter method between the electrical chassis and the electro conductive enclosure/electrical protection barrier shall be less than 0.1 Ω.
condition: if the DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter method is used

text: If lead wires are used for voltage and current measurement, each lead wire shall be independently connected to the electrical protection barrier/enclosure/electrical chassis.
condition: if lead wires are used for voltage and current measurement

text: The isolation resistance for each high voltage bus of the vehicle shall be measured or determined by calculating the measurement values of each part or component unit of the high voltage bus.
All measurements for calculating voltage(s) and electrical isolation shall be made after a minimum of 10 s after the impact.

The isolation resistance measurement shall be conducted by selecting an appropriate method from paragraphs 5.2.1. to 5.2.2. of Annex 11 depending on the electrical charge of the live parts or the isolation resistance, with the range of the electrical circuit to be measured clarified in advance using electrical circuit diagrams.
If the high voltage buses are conductively isolated from each other, isolation resistance shall be measured for each electrical circuit.
condition: if the high voltage buses are conductively isolated from each other

text: Modifications necessary for measuring the isolation resistance (such as removal of the cover to reach live parts, drawing of measurement lines, change in software, or stopping or removing the on-board isolation resistance monitoring device) may be carried out only provided they do not influence the test results.
condition: if modifications are made for the isolation resistance measurement

text: When the on-board isolation resistance monitoring device is removed, a set of drawings shall be used to prove that the isolation resistance between the live parts and the electrical chassis remains unchanged.
condition: if the on-board isolation resistance monitoring device is removed

text: Utmost care shall be exercised to avoid short circuit and electric shock during isolation resistance measurement requiring direct operations of the high-voltage circuit.

For the isolation resistance measurement using DC voltage from external sources, an isolation resistance test instrument capable of applying a DC voltage higher than the working voltage of the high voltage bus shall be used.
condition: if the external DC voltage source method is used

text: For the external DC voltage source method, the isolation resistance test instrument shall be connected between the live parts and the electrical chassis and the isolation resistance measured by applying a DC voltage of at least half of the working voltage of the high voltage bus.
condition: if the external DC voltage source method is used

text: If the system has several voltage ranges in a conductively connected circuit and some components cannot withstand the working voltage of the entire circuit, the isolation resistance between those components and the electrical chassis may be measured separately by applying at least half of their own working voltage with those components disconnected.
condition: if the system has several voltage ranges and some components cannot withstand the working voltage of the entire circuit

text: For the isolation resistance measurement using the vehicle's own REESS, the high voltage bus shall be energized by the vehicle's own REESS and/or energy conversion system, and the voltage level of the REESS and/or energy conversion system throughout the test shall be at least the nominal operating voltage as specified by the vehicle manufacturer.
condition: if the vehicle's own REESS is used as DC voltage source

text: For the isolation resistance measurement using the vehicle's own REESS, the voltmeter shall measure DC values and have an internal resistance of at least 10 MΩ.
condition: if the vehicle's own REESS is used as DC voltage source

text: In the first step, the high voltage bus voltage (Ub) shall be measured and recorded, and Ub shall be equal to or greater than the nominal operating voltage of the REESS and/or energy conversion system as specified by the vehicle manufacturer.
condition: if the vehicle's own REESS is used as DC voltage source

text: In the second step, the voltage (U1) between the negative side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall be measured and recorded.
condition: if the vehicle's own REESS is used as DC voltage source

text: In the third step, the voltage (U2) between the positive side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall be measured and recorded.
condition: if the vehicle's own REESS is used as DC voltage source

text: If U1 is greater than or equal to U2, a standard known resistance (Ro) shall be inserted between the negative side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis, the voltage U1' measured with Ro installed, and the electrical isolation calculated as Ri = Ro*Ub*(1/U1' - 1/U1).
condition: if U1 is greater than or equal to U2

text: If U2 is greater than U1, a standard known resistance (Ro) shall be inserted between the positive side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis, the voltage U2' measured with Ro installed, and the electrical isolation calculated as Ri = Ro*Ub*(1/U2' - 1/U2).
condition: if U2 is greater than U1

text: In the fifth step, the isolation resistance (in Ω/V) shall be obtained by dividing the electrical isolation value Ri (in Ω) by the working voltage of the high voltage bus (in V).
condition: if the vehicle's own REESS is used as DC voltage source

text: The standard known resistance Ro (in Ω) should be the value of the minimum required isolation resistance (Ω/V) multiplied by the working voltage (V) of the vehicle plus/minus 20 per cent.
condition: if the vehicle's own REESS is used as DC voltage source

text: An appropriate coating may be applied, if necessary, to the physical protection (casing) of the REESS in order to confirm if there is any electrolyte leakage from the REESS resulting from the test.
condition: vehicles equipped with electric power train

text: Unless the manufacturer provides means to differentiate between the leakage of different liquids, all liquid leakage shall be considered as the electrolyte.
condition: unless the manufacturer provides means to differentiate between the leakage of different liquids

text: Compliance with the REESS retention requirement shall be determined by visual inspection.
condition: vehicles equipped with electric power train

text: Prior to conducting the crash test, instrumentation is installed in the hydrogen storage system to perform the required pressure and temperature measurements.
condition: if the standard vehicle does not already possess instrumentation with the required accuracy

text: The hydrogen storage system is purged, if necessary, following manufacturer directions to remove impurities from the container before filling the storage system with compressed hydrogen or helium gas.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The target fill pressure shall be determined from the equation Ptarget = NWP x (273 + To) / 288, where NWP is the nominal working pressure (MPa) and To is the ambient temperature to which the storage system is expected to settle.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The hydrogen container is filled to a minimum of 95 per cent of the targeted fill pressure and allowed to settle (stabilize) prior to conducting the crash test.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The main stop valve and shut-off valves for hydrogen gas, located in the downstream hydrogen gas piping, are in the normal driving condition, kept open immediately prior to the impact.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Sensors are selected to measure either the build-up of the hydrogen or helium gas or the reduction in oxygen (due to displacement of air by leaking hydrogen/helium).
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Sensors are calibrated to traceable references to ensure an accuracy of ±5 per cent at the targeted criteria of 4 per cent hydrogen or 3 per cent helium by volume in air.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Sensors shall have a full scale measurement capability of at least 25 per cent above the target criteria.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The sensor shall be capable of a 90 per cent response to a full scale change in concentration within 10 seconds.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Prior to the crash impact, a sensor is located in the passenger compartment at a distance within 250 mm of the headliner above the driver's seat or near the top centre of the passenger compartment.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Prior to the crash impact, a sensor is located at a distance within 250 mm of the floor in front of the rear (or rear most) seat in the passenger compartment.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Prior to the crash impact, a sensor is located at a distance within 100 mm of the top of luggage compartments inside the vehicle that are not directly affected by the particular crash impact to be conducted.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle with luggage compartments not directly affected by the crash impact

text: The sensors are securely mounted on the vehicle structure or seats and protected for the planned crash test from debris, air bag exhaust gas and projectiles.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The measurements following the crash are recorded by instruments located in the vehicle or by remote transmission.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The test may be conducted either outdoors in an area protected from the wind and possible solar effects, or indoors in a space that is large enough or ventilated to prevent the build-up of hydrogen to more than 10 per cent of the targeted criteria in the passenger and luggage compartments.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: For a storage system filled with compressed hydrogen, the hydrogen gas pressure P0 (MPa) and temperature T0 (°C) are measured immediately before the impact and then at a time interval Δt (min) after the impact.
condition: storage system filled with compressed hydrogen

text: For the hydrogen leak test, the time interval Δt starts when the vehicle comes to rest after the impact and continues for at least 60 minutes.
condition: storage system filled with compressed hydrogen

text: The time interval Δt shall be increased if necessary to accommodate measurement accuracy for a storage system with a large volume operating up to 70 MPa; in that case Δt can be calculated as Δt = VCHSS x NWP /1,000 x ((-0.027 x NWP +4) x Rs – 0.21) -1.7 x Rs, where Rs = Ps / NWP.
condition: storage system filled with compressed hydrogen with a large volume operating up to 70 MPa

text: If the calculated value of Δt for the hydrogen leak test is less than 60 minutes, Δt is set to 60 minutes.
condition: if the calculated Δt is less than 60 minutes

text: The initial mass of hydrogen in the storage system is calculated as Po' = Po x 288 / (273 + T0); ρo' = –0.0027 x (P0')2 + 0.75 x P0' + 1.07; Mo = ρo' x VCHSS.
condition: storage system filled with compressed hydrogen

text: The final mass of hydrogen in the storage system Mf at the end of the time interval Δt is calculated as Pf' = Pf x 288 / (273 + Tf); ρf' = –0.0027 x (Pf')2 + 0.75 x Pf' + 1.07; Mf = ρf' x VCHSS, where Pf is the measured final pressure (MPa) and Tf the measured final temperature (°C).
condition: storage system filled with compressed hydrogen

text: The average hydrogen flow rate over the time interval is calculated as VH2 = (Mf-Mo) / Δt x 22.41 / 2.016 x (Ptarget /Po), in NL/min.
condition: storage system filled with compressed hydrogen

text: For a storage system filled with compressed helium, the helium gas pressure P0 (MPa) and temperature T0 (°C) are measured immediately before the impact and then at a predetermined time interval after the impact.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium

text: For the helium leak test, the time interval Δt starts when the vehicle comes to rest after the impact and continues for at least 60 minutes.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium

text: The time interval Δt shall be increased, if necessary, to accommodate measurement accuracy for a storage system with a large volume operating up to 70 MPa; in that case Δt can be calculated as Δt = VCHSS x NWP /1000 x ((-0.028 x NWP +5.5) x Rs – 0.3) – 2.6 x Rs, where Rs = Ps / NWP.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium with a large volume operating up to 70 MPa

text: If the value of Δt for the helium leak test is less than 60 minutes, Δt is set to 60 minutes.
condition: if Δt is less than 60 minutes

text: The initial mass of helium in the storage system is calculated as Po' = Po x 288 / (273 + T0); ρo' = –0.0043 x (P0')2 + 1.53 x P0' + 1.49; Mo = ρo' x VCHSS.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium

text: The final mass of helium in the storage system at the end of the time interval Δt is calculated as Pf' = Pf x 288 / (273 + Tf); ρf' = –0.0043 x (Pf')2 + 1.53 x Pf' + 1.49; Mf = ρf' x VCHSS.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium

text: The average helium flow rate over the time interval is calculated as VHe = (Mf-Mo) / Δt x 22.41 / 4.003 x (Ptarget/ Po), in NL/min.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium

text: The average volumetric flow of helium is converted to the average hydrogen flow by VH2 = VHe / 0.75.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium

text: Post-crash data collection in enclosed spaces commences when the vehicle comes to a rest.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Data from the sensors installed in accordance with paragraph 3.2. of Annex 12 are collected at least every five seconds and continue for a period of 60 minutes after the test.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: A first-order lag (time constant) up to a maximum of five seconds may be applied to the concentration measurements to provide smoothing and filter the effects of spurious data points.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle
